title: But why is a sphere's surface area four times its shadow?
beats: Familiar 4 pi R^2 is a multiple of the circle area; want to feel the four circles, not just prove it
Curvature stops a flat fit; promise two routes (Archimedes, his own shadow route) plus generalization
Bird's eye: sphere equals cylinder label, unwrap to rectangle 2 pi R by 2R, giving the formula
Four circles will fit in later; first, why sphere relates to cylinder
Project tiny rectangles outward like shadows; area stays equal
Two competing effects: width stretched, height squished like a tilted object's shadow; they cancel
Name r and d; similar triangles give width scale R/d
Height squish: tangent perpendicular to radius, similar triangles, also R/d; do not take my word, justify it yourself
Fun coincidence: projection looks like 90 degree rotation, giving odd rearrangement animation
Rectangles only approximate; finer covering shows both limits equal, doubling as a definition of area
This is calculus without jargon; good primer before definitions
Unwrap circles to triangles (earlier calculus video), four fit in rectangle
Second proof as 5 guided exercises; pause and predict (rings vs ring shadows, theta, d-theta)
Any convex shape: average shadow is one quarter surface area; proof deferred

theory: He states the shape of the argument (two effects that cancel) before computing anything, so each triangle step is checkable against a known destination. Rigor arrives as names and similar triangles, and the learner is then handed the second proof as exercises. The honest admission that lectures are weaker than doing is itself the pedagogy.
velocity: Orchestrator: when a proof is long, play a 'rough sketch' beat first with the claim in words.
Scene builder: ready-made 3D-to-2D cross-section toggle and rectangle projection animation.
Voice: pause for prediction at 'challenge mode' moments; wait, do not fill silence.
Learner model: switch from lecture to guided exercises when the learner has shown competence.
Evals: check that a heuristic tip ('tangent is perpendicular to radius') is offered at the stuck point.
